assessment_summary: Step 0024 incorrectly distributes the expression in 0020. In a distributive lattice, $(x \vee b) \wedge (x \vee a) = x \vee (b \wedge a)$. The text incorrectly claims this simplifies to $(m \vee n) \wedge (b \vee a)$ instead of $(m \vee n) \vee (b \wedge a)$, swapping the meet and join operators. This deduction is mathematically invalid.
counterexample: Let L be the boolean lattice {0, 1}. Let F = {1} and M = {0}. Let m = 0, n = 0, a = 1, b = 1. Then m \vee a = 1 \in F and n \vee b = 1 \in F. Step 0020 evaluates to ((0 \vee 0) \vee 1) \wedge ((0 \vee 0) \vee 1) = 1 \wedge 1 = 1 \in F. But step 0024 evaluates to (0 \vee 0) \wedge (1 \vee 1) = 0 \wedge 1 = 0 \notin F. Thus 0024 does not logically follow from 0020.
